The '''Alpha-3 ''Nimbus''-class V-wing starfighter''', often simply known as the ''' V-wing starfighter''' or '''Nimbus fighter''', was a short-ranged [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] deployed late in the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].

V-wings were some of the more recent spacecraft in the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]], and frequently filled the role as combat support ships. The small silhouette, high speed, and great agility of this fighter made it hard to target and a very effective ship despite its small size. They were later succeeded by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE Fighter]] and [[TIE series/Legends|its variants]], as well as the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] [[RZ-1 A-wing interceptor/Legends|RZ-1 A-wing interceptor]], all of which incorporated aspects of the V-wing into their designs.

==Characteristics==
[[File:CloneFlightSquadSevenVwings.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Republic V-wing starfighters over Coruscant.]]
The Alpha-3 ''Nimbus''-class starfighter was a sturdy, wedge-shaped [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] similar to the [[Delta-7 Aethersprite-class light interceptor/Legends|Delta-7 ''Aethersprite''-class interceptors]] used by the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]. It was manufactured by [[Kuat Systems Engineering/Legends|Kuat Systems Engineering]], the same company responsible for both the Delta-7 fighter and its successor, the [[Eta-2 Actis-class interceptor/Legends|Eta-2 ''Actis''-class interceptor]], and was designed as a successor to the [[V-19 Torrent starfighter/Legends|V-19 Torrent starfighter]]<ref name="dbvw" /> by [[Slayn & Korpil/Legends|Slayn & Korpil]].<ref name="db">{{DB|starship|v19torrent|V-19 Torrent starfighter}}</ref> Both the Delta-7 and the Alpha-3 were designed by the engineer [[Walex Blissex/Legends|Walex Blissex]],<ref name="dbvw" /> who would later co-design the Rebel Alliance's [[RZ-1 A-wing interceptor/Legends|A-wing fighter]] with [[Jan Dodonna/Legends|Jan Dodonna]].<ref name="RAS">''[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook]]''</ref>

The V-Wing featured folding wings similar to those fitted on the later Eta-2 interceptors. But when landing, the wings fold downward to form as landing gear. On each wing was a radiator panel which helped aid in heat disposal during combat. Nestled between each wing and the hull were two twin [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannons]], which could swivel on the vessel's wing hubs to provide a wide range of fire.<ref name="ROTS:ICS" /> A single forward [[Concussion missile launcher/Legends|concussion missile launcher]] could be fitted to the prow.<ref name="SoT" /> Aft of the starfighter's main hull were two [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shield]] heat sinks, located above the two vertically stacked [[Ion engine/Legends|ion drive]] thrusters. These flaps also provided some protection for the V-wing's [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]]s.<ref name="ROTS:ICS" /> Some models were equipped with [[Flak gun/Legends|Flak guns]] and [[Proton bomb/Legends|Proton bombs]].<ref name="PrimaBF2">[[Star Wars Battlefront II: Prima Official Game Guide|''Star Wars Battlefront II'': Prima Official Game Guide]]</ref> 

[[File:Vwing_ICS.jpg|thumb|left|240px|V-wing cross-section.]]

In keeping with the design of the Delta-7, the Alpha-3 featured an [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] [[Astromech socket/Legends|socket]] aft of the oval cockpit. V-wing pilots were often assisted by spherical [[Q7-series astromech droid/Legends|Q7-series astromech droids]] which provided in-flight navigation and maintenance skills that would otherwise require a copilot&mdash;which the compact V-wing could not accommodate.<ref name="ROTS:ICS" /> However, later incarnations of the V-wing used by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] omitted the astromech, with the pilot as the only occupant.<ref name="LC2">[[Darth Vader and the Lost Command 2|''Darth Vader and the Lost Command'' 2]]</ref> In addition, some later incarnations utilized a similar engine to the later [[TIE series/Legends|TIE Series]], resulting in it having a similar engine roar to its successors.<ref name="RotS" />

The V-wing starfighter was too small to feature an integrated [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]], and like their Jedi-owned counterparts, it required transportation into combat zones by carriers such as the [[Venator-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Venator''-class Star Destroyers]].<ref name="ROTS:ICS" /> Additionally, V-wing fighters were also capable of using [[Syliure-45 hyperdrive module/Legends|Syluire-45 hyperspace transport rings]] to go long distances like the Eta-2 and both Delta-7 models.

==History==
V-wing fighters were often unleashed from warship hangars in large swarms, and were one of the most numerous starfighters in the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]] late in the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. They were most frequently deployed from ''Venator''-class Star Destroyers and were typically the primary fighter aboard these vessels. While they lacked the power of the [[Aggressive ReConnaissance-170 starfighter/Legends|ARC-170 starfighter]], they made up for it in raw speed and agility. There were produced in limited numbers until [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]]. V-wings were speedy and evasive targets, even for the advanced [[Droid tri-fighter/Legends|droid tri-fighters]] used by the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] in the last days of the Clone Wars. Mass-produced for Loyalist forces, V-wings participated in large-scale fleet operations and assisted in the defense of [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] worlds during the Clone Wars. They were <ref name="ROTS:ICS" /> The [[Clone trooper pilot/Legends|clone trooper pilots]] who flew the fighter had specially adapted [[Helmet/Legends|helmets]], differing from the ones usually worn by other clone pilots. These round helmets fully enclosed the wearer's face and, along with their [[Flight suit/Legends|flight suits]], were fully sealed due to the lack of a [[Life support/Legends|life support]] system. These suits allowed them to survive in space after ejection. The same pilot suit was also worn by the pilots of [[Theta-class T-2c shuttle/Legends|''Theta''-class T-2c shuttles]].<ref name="ROTS:ICS" />

V-wing starfighters flew into battle alongside ARC-170s and Eta-2 interceptors during the [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|Battle of Coruscant]] near the end of the conflict, fighting off droid tri-fighters, [[Vulture-class starfighter/Legends|Vulture droids]], and deadly [[Pistoeka sabotage droid/Legends|buzz droids]], with some even getting as far as the Separatist flagship, [[Invisible Hand/Legends|''Invisible Hand'']], although many were lost to enemy fire.

Following the end of the Clone Wars, V-wing squadrons flew under the banner of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="dbvw" /> Three<ref name="RotS" /> [[Experimental V-wing]]s, flown by elite pilots,<ref name="dbvw" /> escorted the self-appointed [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] [[Theta-class T-2c shuttle/Legends|shuttle]] during his voyage from [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] to [[Mustafar/Legends|Mustafar]] and again on the return trip, culminating at the [[Emperor Palpatine Surgical Reconstruction Center]].<ref name="RotS" /> These elite V-wings were modified for [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] travel<ref name="dbvw" /> and equipped with upgraded shields. In the early stages of the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]], new V-wing models were commissioned. These craft featured Imperial livery and lacked an astromech droid.<ref name="LC2" /> The clone pilots wore a completely black flight suit with a life support system and a black helmet similar to the ones worn by the earlier clone pilots of ARC-170 starfighters, but with parts of their face being exposed and and goggles covering their eyes.<ref name="Tin Collection">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: 30th Anniversary Collection|packtype=Commemorative Tin Collection|pack=Star Wars: Episode III - Revenge of the Sith (Exclusive Edition) (Clone Commander Cody, Anakin Skywalker, General Grievous. Clone Pilot)|altlink=https://www.jeditemplearchives.com/content/modules.php?name=JReviews&rop=showcontent&id=1878}}</ref> Eventually, most of them were phased out in favor of the [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE Fighter]] and [[TIE series/Legends|its variants]], and were either scrapped or sold for surplus.<ref name="SoT" />

At least several V-wings would fall into the hands of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].
[[File:Eaw_alpha3_V-wing.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Three V-wings in service of pirates during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].]]
Eventually, private organizations, such as the [[Hutt Cartel/Legends|Hutt Cartel]], used V-wings after salvaging them. They were also used by the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]] around the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]] during a [[Skirmish over Mandalore|skirmish]] with the [[Zann Consortium/Legends|Zann Consortium]].<ref name="FoC" />

In [[13 ABY/Legends|13 ABY]],<ref name="Date">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates the events of [[Star Wars: Crimson Empire II: Council of Blood|''Crimson Empire II: Council of Blood'']] to [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]]. According to {{SWArchive|url=vault/books/crimsonempire3/index.html|text=Back in the Red: Dark Horse Comics Announces Long-Awaited Crimson Empire III Series}}, the events of[[Star Wars: Crimson Empire III: Empire Lost|''Star Wars: Crimson Empire III—Empire Lost'']] take place two years after those of ''Council of Blood'', in 13 ABY.</ref> they were one of many Clone Wars-era vehicles used by the [[Restored Empire]]. Several V-wings were present at the Imperial faction's [[RZ7-6113-23 base|base]] on the [[class-6 planetoid]] [[RZ7-6113-23]] for the arrival of former [[Emperor's Royal Guard/Legends|Imperial Guardsman]] [[Kir Kanos]]<ref name="EL1" />

The Restored Empire's V-wings later saw action against a [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] force investigating the [[Ambush at RZ7-6113-23|disappearance]] of the ''[[Endor (Dauntless-class)|Endor]]'' over RZ7-6113-23. The ''Nimbus''-class starfighters [[Battle of RZ7-6113-23|engaged]] the [[MC80 Liberty Type Heavy Star Cruiser/Legends|MC80 Star Cruiser]] of [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Lar Ndigo]] to buy time for the Restored Empire's fleet to launch, losing at least two of their number to the [[Cruiser/Legends|cruiser's]] complement of [A-wing interceptors.<ref name="EL4">[[Crimson Empire III: Empire Lost 4|''Crimson Empire III: Empire Lost'' 4]]</ref> The faction once again employed V-wing starfighters in an [[Battle of Orinda (13 ABY)|attack]] on the insufficiently-defended [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]] [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Orinda/Legends|Orinda]]. The Restored Empire's numerical superiority made short work of the [[Planet/Legends|planet's]] defenses, with the outdated V-wings seeing success against the more modern [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE/LN starfighters]].<ref name="EL5">[[Crimson Empire III: Empire Lost 5|''Crimson Empire III: Empire Lost'' 5]]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:V-Wing.jpg|thumb|right|280px|Concept art]]
The Alpha-3 ''Nimbus''-class V-wing starfighter was designed for the film [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars:'' Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']] directed by [[George Lucas]].<ref name="RotS" /> Prior to the release of the film on [[May 19]], [[2005]],<ref name="Year by Year">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, Updated and Expanded Edition]]''</ref> the V-wings appeared in the novel ''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]'' by [[James Luceno]], released on [[January 25]],<ref name="Labyrinth">''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]''</ref> and were described and identified in the reference book ''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith Incredible Cross-Sections]]'',<ref name="ROTS:ICS" /> released on [[April 2]].<ref name="Planning">{{SWArchive|url=episode-iii/release/publishing/news20041124.html|text=Planning Your Episode III Bookshelf}}</ref>

===Further appearances and discrepancies===
In the games ''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]'' and ''[[Star Wars Battlefront: Renegade Squadron]]'',<ref name="BF:RS" /> the V-wing is depicted as a heavy [[Bomber/Legends|bomber]] with [[shock cannon]]s and proton bombs rather than the fast interceptor craft that it has been established as in other sources. Although this portrayal of the ship is likely considered non-canon, it was done regardless as the fighter and interceptor roles for the Republic faction were already filled, leaving the V-wing to take on the bomber ship class. Surprisingly, the ARC-170, which has a role of bomber in other sources, does not have that same role in ''Battlefront II''&mdash;it is given the multi-purpose fighter role, likely for the purpose of creating continuity with its better-known descendant, the [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing]]. The V-wing was also a ship in which players of the now closed MMO ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]'' could fly as their personal ship. However, it was a very rare ship as it was only available as a loot card in the ''[[Squadrons Over Corellia]]'' trading card game booster packs. Due to the rarity of this ship in ''Star Wars Galaxies'' it was highly sought after by pilots who actively took part in player versus player content in space. A V-wing can be found on [[Raxus Prime/Legends|Raxus Prime]] in ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]'' on the Nintendo DS version of the game. In the video game ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]'', V-Wings are used by pirate space forces, however their icon is the same of that of the [[Z-95 Headhunter/Legends|Z-95 Headhunter's]]. This is fixed in the sequel. In ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption]]'', during the [[Mission to Mandalore (Zann Consortium)|Mission to Mandalore]], there are V-wings used by the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]] that have ion cannons. When [[Hasbro]] designed the V-wing action vehicle, the folding wings were not fully incorporated into use as landing gear as was shown in ''Revenge of the Sith''.

===Non-canon appearances===
Multiple [[LEGO Star Wars|LEGO ''Star Wars'']] sets of V-wings were released. The first set was released in [[2006]] as part of the ''Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith'' line and included minifigures of a clone pilot and Q7-series astromech droid.<ref name="LEGO 6205">{{LEGOCite|num=6205|name=V-Wing Fighter}}</ref> In the newer line of LEGO ''Star Wars'' products in January of [[2011]], a new set called the "Imperial V-Wing Starfighter" was released. This set includes a black version of the V-wing fighter, and a minifigure<ref name="LEGO 7915">{{LEGOCite|num=7915|name=Imperial V-wing Starfighter}}</ref> of an original Imperial V-Wing Pilot design with a fully black colored variant of the uniform of the craft's clone pilots,<ref name="2015 LEGO CE">''[[LEGO Star Wars Character Encyclopedia: Updated and Expanded]]''</ref> as well as [[R2-Q2/Legends|R2-Q2]].<ref name="LEGO 7915" /> Another LEGO release of the Republic V-wing came out in January [[2014]], with a clone pilot and an unnamed red astromech droid as minifigures included in the set.<ref name="LEGO 75039">{{LEGOCite|num=75039|name=V-Wing Starfighter}}</ref>
